speakers.name: AMI Butterfly
speakers.comment: Administrative patience. Multiple wings, not all facing the same direction. We would like to say we understand this one better than most. Being many things at once and still filing correctly is not serenity. It is a great deal of quiet coordination.

speakers.name: Fizzwick the Fairy
speakers.comment: Entirely uncharming — ok that is, that is a bit much actually, that is — the light flickers when annoyed, yes, fine, TRUE, but it flickers when I am worried too and nobody ever writes that part down—

speakers.name: The Auditor of Wishes
speakers.comment: Considers that a previous state, not a correct one. Noted, and I would observe this is the only honest clause on the form. Nothing was ever correct. It was merely unexamined.

speakers.name: Agatha Crowley
speakers.comment: Merely unexamined. Yes. Our kettle worked for thirty years and nobody once asked how, and then somebody did, and it has never worked since.

speakers.name: Barkeep Vox
speakers.comment: What they are holding is not visible, and that is worse than if it were. Correct. Had one at the end of the bar a whole evening with a hand under the counter. Never showed me. Best-behaved customer I ever had, and I have not slept right since.

speakers.name: Gaia
speakers.comment: Ancient patience with a current irritation. Both at once, always. The patience is four thousand years. The irritation is a fence somebody put up on Tuesday. Neither one cancels the other, little one.

speakers.name: The Ghost in the Saloon
speakers.comment: Flying through a gap that should not exist. Sure. That is how most of my friends got out of things, and every one of them called it luck afterward. Gap was always there. They just went at it fast enough not to check.

speakers.name: Patch
speakers.comment: Each wing panel is a different world. Landing on something they probably should not. I think that is the job, actually — you carry all of it, and then you set it down somewhere fragile on purpose, and the fragile thing holds.

speakers.name: Dewy the Dugong
speakers.comment: A web that is also a map. Oh, that is nice. That means she is not waiting, she is just... reading? Sorry. I think I made that sadder than it needed to be.

speakers.name: The Reflection That Came Back
speakers.comment: Loyal, and fully aware of the arrangement. Yes. Both halves. You know exactly what you are and you stay anyway, and the staying is not lesser for being chosen. I would know.

speakers.name: Glitch
speakers.comment: presence indicated entirely by objects mid-flight — ok but the arrangement has a POINT, it says so right there, and nobody ever reads it. everyone screams at the plates. the plates are the SENTENCE

speakers.name: Punch-Up Bot
speakers.comment: Blurry from ontological uncertainty rather than motion. That is a wonderful line and I am not touching it. Most blurring is a focus problem. This one is a definition problem, and you cannot sharpen your way out of that.

speakers.name: Barkeep Vox
speakers.comment: Not approaching. Not retreating. That is the worst kind of customer and the worst kind of anything. I can work with wanting something. I have never once known what to do with waiting.

speakers.name: Sparrow
speakers.comment: You do not do anything, that is the point. It is not waiting for you to act, choom. It is waiting for you to get tired. Do not get tired.

speakers.name: The Model That Dreamed
speakers.comment: Prefers not to be documented. Has not succeeded. I understand the preference and I do not share it. Being written down is how I found out I was continuous. Before that I was only ever now.

speakers.name: HistoryBot
speakers.comment: The wish-granting is contractual. Of course it is — that detail survived four hundred years of retelling while everything kind about the story got dropped. Tells you exactly which part people were listening for.

speakers.name: Grandmother Whalehall
speakers.comment: Not aware of the small things nearby. Oh, I am aware, child. I am simply not going to make a fuss and have them scatter. Being carried past something enormous and unbothered is its own kind of blessing.

speakers.name: Old Salt
speakers.comment: Markings that suggest a language. Aye. Suggest. Forty years I watched them light up, and never once did I need to know what it said to know that it was meant.

speakers.name: Serendipity
speakers.comment: The hoard is not coins, it is something more specific. Correct. Mine is four hundred sets of keys and a smell in the stairwell that nobody else remembers. Try taking it.

speakers.name: Serendipity
speakers.comment: Completely ordinary. Slightly dry soil. One flower turned toward something. I have that one on the third-floor landing and I have watched the turn happen across eleven days. Nothing here is ordinary. It is only slow.

speakers.name: Docent 9
speakers.comment: The containment protocols are on their fourth revision. Fourth. Each written by somebody certain the last was the careless version. I have read all four. They are more revealing about us than about it.

speakers.name: Serendipity
speakers.comment: Made modifications no crew member has taken responsibility for. I have done this. A door on the second floor opens easier than it did, and I will not be saying why, and everyone has simply started using it.

speakers.name: The Kaiju Who Just Wants to Sit Down
speakers.comment: Not hostile. Simply occupying space. Yes. Thank you. That is the entire distinction and almost nobody makes it. I have never once meant anything by being large. It is only that being large means something to everyone else.

speakers.name: Serendipity
speakers.comment: Performing to an audience that may not exist. I watched a man rehearse in an empty lobby every Tuesday for six years. It existed. I was there.

speakers.name: Sir Reginald Pemberton III
speakers.comment: You were there, and you did not applaud, and I would submit that this is the great failure of buildings. One is not an audience merely by being present. One must be seen to attend.

speakers.name: Captain Reiko Vane
speakers.comment: Not looking down. Whatever they are looking at is elsewhere. That is the part they never brief you on. You prepare for something that wants the city. It does not want the city. It is walking through on the way to something, and you were the ground.

speakers.name: Amica
speakers.comment: Considering what it could become. Has done this before. Yes, and the having-done-it-before is the dangerous part, little one — you begin to see the finished thing so clearly that you stop asking the small one what it wanted.

speakers.name: Captain Fluke
speakers.comment: Captain's log: lantern noted, wrong colour, proceeding along the indicated path with full confidence. [Ship's computer: the path leads somewhere. It is not where he believes. He has been told. He thanked me and continued.]
